newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - March 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - March 18.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Democrat Party MP Suthep Thaugsuban has said he has in his possession stunning evidence which proves certain Cabinet members and coalition members of parliament received money during the last general election from Rakesh Saxena, a key suspect in the Bangkok Bank of Commerce (BBC) fraud scandal. Suthep would not name the Cabinet members outright, but asked Deputy Interior Minister Chalerm Yoobamrung and Deputy Prime Minister Samak Sundaravej to pursue their earlier requests for a special House meeting to debate the case. (THE NATION)

- Police Director General Pracha Promnok has ordered a lightning and unprecedented purge of 58 Highway Police division officers following much-publicised allegations that the division has received bribes from trucking firms. The highway division purge included all five deputy commanders of the division and at least 10 deputy inspectors in charge of monitoring road check-points. (THE NATION)

- Forum of the Poor representatives have walked out of their meeting with Agriculture Ministry officials after their talks over land and forest disputes in the North became deadlocked. The talks were called to settle grievances of northern hilltribe villagers facing eviction from highlands they claimed to have occupied before they were declared first-class watershed areas. (BANGKOK POST)

- Additional licences for nine finance firms, which do not have all four licences necessary for full-service operation, have been approved by the Screening Committee on Economic Affairs. However, Deputy Prime Minister and Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan refuses to disclose the names of the nine firms. (BUSINESS DAY)

- The long-pending natural gas purchase deal with the Malaysia-Thai Joint Development Area (JDA) may be cancelled by the Petroleum Authority of Thailand (PTT), as the two sides have not been able to reach a compromise decision regarding the pricing. The deal for PTT to buy natural gas from JDA is unlikely to materialise as PTT can not accept the price as well as other conditions proposed by its Malaysian counterpart. (BUSINESS DAY)

- Foreign investors in Thailand will be allowed to buy housing for their staff without restriction. Regulations reserving certain businesses for Thais will be eased, and refunds of import tax and value-added tax on exports will be speeded up. (BANGKOK POST)
